summary:
D2 and D3 are built. Backend tsc and admin tsc are both clean. All 118 tests pass in the 7 suites I ran.

**D2: the CEO section**
- `lib/workspaces.ts` has a new `ceo` workspace, listed first, owned by `admin` only. Its sections are:
  - Overview: `ceo_overview`
  - Approvals: new module `approvals`
  - Companies & head offices: `tenants`, `business_info`, `onboarding`
  - Logins & access: `role_management`, `role_modules`
  - Company rules: `configuration`, `settings`
- The old Operations "company" section is gone, so each module id is still in exactly one workspace (tested).
- Operations is now owned by `fnb_manager`. The CEO (admin) still holds every module, so it still sees everything.
- PPL-09 still holds: `setup/routes.ts` gives rule-edit rights to the owners of whichever workspace holds `configuration`. That workspace is now the CEO-only one, so the editors are still admin plus owner. A test pins this.
- `moduleAccess.ts`:
  - `approvals` is added to MODULE_IDS. owner, management and legacy manager pick it up automatically, because their defaults are "every module except …".
  - `approvals` is added to MODULE_GRANTS, so saved rows for those three roles get it once.
  - Every other role's defaults are byte-for-byte unchanged (pinned in accessControl.test).
  - No new gated prefix: the inbox grants nothing by itself.

**D3: one approvals inbox**
- New `backend/src/modules/approvals/`, exporting `registerApprovalsPlugin(api)`. It serves `GET /approvals` (counts per type plus items, with an optional `?type=` filter) and `GET /approvals/counts`.
- It is read-only and has no approvals table. Each type reads its module's existing queue route as the signed-in user, via `fastify.inject` with the same session and company headers only. So the module's own role guard, Module Access switch and company scope all apply.
  - If that route answers 401/403/404, the type disappears from that person's inbox.
  - Items are then kept only for the companies in view (`resolveTenantScope`), so counts are per company.
  - These internal reads count as internal traffic, so they don't use up the user's rate limit.
- Each item carries the module's existing approve/reject route (method, path, body, and a reason/note field where the route takes one). The page calls those routes directly.
- `approverRoles` copies each approve route's role list. It only narrows what is shown, never widens it.
- Types:
  - new logins (admin)
  - website changes (admin; publish now, or send back with a note)
  - purchase orders over the limit (admin; reason required to reject)
  - recipes (admin and owner; an owner's own submissions are hidden)
  - HR requests (per step, from `/hr/approvals`)
  - payroll drafts (admin, owner, management; whoever prepared it is excluded unless admin)
  - tip pools (admin and owner; link to the module only, because posting needs review)
  - stock transfers (all managers; approve or cancel)
- Left out on purpose, because they have no request state: period reopen, manual journals, journal reversal, capex posting, bank-line adjustments and the till's manager-PIN overrides. The README explains why.
- Delegation: `delegations.ts` has an `ApprovalDelegations.typesFor()` hook, checked per type, which returns nothing today. The README notes that each module's approve and queue routes must also accept a delegate before a hand-over works.

**Admin screens**
- `/ceo` is the CEO section home: approvals counts plus the section cards.
- `/ceo/approvals` is the inbox:
  - type chips with counts
  - per item: key facts, company label in All-companies view, time waiting
  - inline buttons, with the item's company pinned on writes
  - HR requests open in the same `RecordDetail` view the old page used (overtime hours, swaps, notes)
  - a link into each module's own screen
- `/hr/approvals` now redirects to `/ceo/approvals?type=hr_request`.
- `moduleCatalog.ts`:
  - `approvals` entry added, and the `configuration` module's main page is now "Company rules" (`/configuration/operations`).
  - The personal "My approvals" link is now "Approvals" → `/ceo/approvals`.
- AppShell:
  - New counts badge on Approvals.
  - The personal Approvals link shows only when the CEO section doesn't already list it for you.
  - The two CEO-only identity-card badges are replaced by one "N waiting on you" link, shown to anyone with something waiting.
  - The CEO header's "home" link goes to `/ceo`.

**Not done or registered:** nothing is registered in `index.ts`. W4 needs to call `await registerApprovalsPlugin(api)` from `/api/v1`. No schema changes, no commits.
tests:
Backend `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` is clean, and so is frontend/admin `npx tsc --noEmit -p .`.

vitest against servd_test_ceo: 7 files, 118 tests, all passing:
- approvalsInbox: 14 (new)
- workspaces: 14 (5 new D2 tests)
- accessControl: 28 (3 new: unchanged defaults for uninvolved roles, governance roles gain only `approvals`, inbox not module-gated)
- auditPeopleAccess: 7 (1 new)
- preBills: 24
- connectorsRoutes: 20
- connectorsWhatsapp: 11 (run because MODULE_GRANTS changed)

auditAccounting and brandReconcile, which also read the workspaces, pass too.

approvalsInbox covers:
- Company B's CEO and HOD never see company A's items.
- Counts are per company, and "All companies" view adds both companies together.
- Exact type lists per role (owner, management, hr, fnb_manager, foh_management, a HOD, and every floor/finance/marketing/it role gets none).
- An owner never sees their own recipe.
- An owner denied the payroll module gets no tip pools.
- Inline approve goes through the existing routes and their guards still apply: PO approve (owner 403, other company 404, CEO 200, then the item leaves the inbox), the HOD's decide on an HR request (other company 404, step advances to HR), stock transfer (cashier 403, F&B manager 200), and staff login approve (management 403, other company 404).
- `?type=` validation, 401 without a session, and a provider failure flagged rather than fatal.
- All of it runs with the plugin registered under /api/v1 through registerApprovalsPlugin.

No `next build` or dev server was run.

ownerQuestions:
1. The F&B manager now owns Operations but by default does not hold the 'procurement' (buying) module. Should it? I did not add it: MODULE_GRANTS is keyed by module only, so a grant would also re-add procurement to the saved rows of every role where the CEO had unticked it. Adding it needs a per-role grant.
2. Owner, management and the legacy manager hold the company modules today, so they now see a section titled "CEO" holding those same pages (plus Approvals). Should that section have a different name for them, or should owner and management lose some of those modules by default?
3. Should tip pools be approvable inline from the inbox? Today they only link to /tip-pools, because posting checks hours and may need kiosk staff left out by name.
4. Stock transfers show for every manager tier (the route lets them all approve), including the person who requested it. Should requesting and approving be split between two people, as purchase orders and recipes are?
